title: C_static extraction report — v1.0
description: plan.md §9, chainlink #24. One generated report per crate, at ci/results/c_static/<report_id>.json, holding the realized-call (C_static) observation for one configuration: the call sites discovered, their honest resolution class (definite-direct-call / possible-dispatch / unresolved-indirect-call), the scope the extractor can actually speak for (coverage_scope), the configuration the observation is relative to (config_scope, the same shape as an interaction's realization.config_scope so R1 can compare them directly), and what the extractor could NOT attribute (attribution_scope). This is an OBSERVATION, never a normative artifact: it carries no `review` block and is never routed through draft/approve -- it is regenerated from source, and a promoted spec is never derived from it. Reconciling it against I (R1) and applying the unresolved risk policy (G16) is scripts/gate_r1_g16.py's job, not this schema's -- the same boundary #16 drew for R2 and #22 drew for harness generation.

report_id.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, enforced by scripts/validate_callsites.py), the same discipline as boundary_id/interaction_id/bridge_id.

crate_dir.description: Workspace-relative crate directory this report was extracted from -- the descriptor's own crates[].crate_dir value, so the gate can resolve which crate's _interactions/ this report reconciles against.

callsites.description: Every discovered call site, in source order. May be empty -- a crate with no attributable call sites is a real, honest result, and its callsite_coverage says so.

coverage_scope.description: plan.md §9's coverage_scope block: what this extractor can speak for, and how strongly. The extractor_backing/completeness_claim pair is the structural form of chainlink #24's 'no regex-only completeness claim' -- see the conditional below.

extractor_backing.description: How the extractor knows what it knows. `syntactic` = a source-level lexer/structural pass with no name resolution or type information. `compiler` = backed by a real compiler front end (rustc/MIR), which is what plan.md §9 defers to 'later, for release-critical clusters or disputed edges'.

unsupported_call_forms.description: Call forms this extractor cannot see at all -- distinct from forms it sees but cannot resolve (those become possible-dispatch / unresolved-indirect-call call sites, which ARE in the report). May be empty only if the extractor genuinely has no blind spot.

completeness_claim.description: `discovered-lower-bound`: these call sites exist; others may exist that were not discovered. `sound-for-supported-forms`: every call site of a supported form IS in this report -- a soundness claim only a compiler-backed extractor may make (see the if/then below).

allOf.description: chainlink #24, structurally: 'no regex-only completeness claim'. A syntactic extractor has no name resolution, so it cannot know it saw everything -- it may only claim a lower bound. Only a compiler-backed extractor may assert soundness for its supported forms. Encoded here rather than left to a validator so no future extractor can quietly promote its own claim.

config_scope.description: The configuration this observation is relative to. Same shape and same target pattern as docs/interaction-schema.json's realization.config_scope, deliberately -- R1 compares the two directly ('realized calls matching within compatible configurations', plan.md §12), and a divergent shape would make that comparison guesswork.

attribution_scope.description: What the extractor looked inside, which concepts it considers in-scope, and what it saw but could not attribute to a source-level method identity. These counts are the honest complement of `callsites`: they exist so an omission is visible and counted rather than silently absent from the report.

local_concepts.description: The concept universe this report is scoped to: every type with an impl block in the scanned sources. C is a relation between local concept methods, so a call whose callee cannot be any of these is out of the graph's domain (counted in out_of_scope_call_sites), not an unresolved edge -- tiering `HashMap::new()` as a medium-risk unresolved call site would bury the real dispatch risk in noise. Recorded here so the scoping decision is auditable rather than implicit.

unattributed_call_sites.description: Call-shaped expressions found outside any scanned item kind (free functions, trait default bodies, impls on foreign or non-concept-shaped types, const initializers). Counted, never attributed -- a caller role needs a concept, and inventing one would be a fabricated method identity.

out_of_scope_call_sites.description: Call sites inside a scanned method whose callee cannot be any local concept method (see local_concepts) -- calls into std, other crates, or free functions. Out of C's domain by construction, not unresolved edges.

macro_invocations.description: Macro invocations encountered. A macro can expand to calls that are not present in the source token stream at all; this count makes that blind spot visible.

callsite_coverage.description: plan.md §9's callsite_coverage, with one deliberate rename: plan's `checked` is a RECONCILIATION outcome (was this call site checked against I?), which extraction cannot know -- scripts/gate_r1_g16.py computes and reports `checked`. What extraction knows is source-level resolution, so this block reports `resolved`. All three counts are recomputed from `callsites` and rejected on disagreement (G1b, scripts/validate_callsites.py) -- never trusted as stored, the same discipline computed eligibility applies in I.

resolved.description: Call sites with call_class definite-direct-call -- resolved to a source-level method identity.

unresolved.description: possible-dispatch + unresolved-indirect-call. plan.md §9: report 'all discovered call sites resolved' when this is 0. Never 'all call sites resolved'.

callsite_id.description: plan.md §9's own shape (CS-SCHED-DISPATCH-004). Deterministic from caller concept/method plus a 1-based occurrence index within that method, so re-extraction of unchanged source produces the same ids and a human-set risk tier can be carried over (extract_c_static.py --previous).

call_class.description: plan.md §9's three classes, exactly. definite-direct-call: callee resolved to a concept method at source level. possible-dispatch: the method name is known, the receiver type is not -- may be a dynamic dispatch. unresolved-indirect-call: the callee cannot be named at all (call through a value, a binding indistinguishable from a fn pointer or closure without name resolution).

callee_method.description: possible-dispatch only: the method name is known even though the receiving concept is not. Never promoted to a `callee` role -- naming a concept the extractor did not resolve would be a fabricated edge.

unresolved_expression.description: The call expression as it appears in source, for the two unresolved classes -- what a human needs to adjudicate the risk tier.

risk_tier.description: plan.md §9.1: critical/high block, medium is a human decision, low is a visible accepted limitation. Required on the two unresolved classes, forbidden on definite-direct-call (a resolved call has no unresolved risk to tier).

risk_tier_source.description: Where risk_tier came from. The extractor only ever emits `extractor-default` with tier `medium` -- it has no basis for critical/high, and `low` would silently accept a limitation nobody looked at. Moving a tier off the default is a human decision and carries its own review block.

required_bridges.description: plan.md §9's own field: bridge_ids a checker must discharge at this call site. Populated by later Stage 8A work (#47 harness generation), not by extraction.

allOf.description: A human-set tier carries its own review block; an extractor default must not carry one, since no human signed off on it.

source.description: plan.md §9's source block, plus `line`. syntax_hash -- not the line number -- is the stable anchor: it hashes the enclosing method's comment- and literal-stripped token text, so reformatting or an edit elsewhere in the file does not invalidate it.

role.description: Identical to docs/interaction-schema.json's own role definition -- R1 matches C roles against I roles, so the two vocabularies must not drift.
